GLM.title: GLM-5.3 - Overview - Z.AI DEVELOPER DOCUMENT
GLM.description: [_jsx(Tip,{children:_jsxs(_components.p,{children:[`GLM-5.3 is now available to all GLM Coding Plan users, with 50% better coding performance! ` ... [_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`GLM-5.3`}),` is Z.ai’s latest flagship model...
GLM.content:
GLM-5.3 is Z.ai’s latest flagship model, delivering comprehensive advancements in complex software engineering and agent capabilities. It uses the same base model as GLM-5.2, with all improvements driven by post-training. Compared with GLM-5.2, it delivers significantly stronger performance in complex programming and long-horizon tasks:Stronger Coding CapabilityGLM-5.3 delivers a significant improvement in coding capabilities, achieving a 50% performance gain over GLM-5.2 on Z.ai Code Bench. It also reaches state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance among open-source models on public benchmarks, including Terminal Bench 3.0 and Agents’ Last Exam (CLI).Emergent Cyber CapabilityAs the scale of post-training continues to expand, the model’s cybersecurity capabilities have improved at a rate that exceeds expectations. GLM-5.3 achieves the best performance to date on the CyberGym vulnerability discovery benchmark. Moreover, the deeper it progresses along the vulnerability exploitation chain, the more pronounced its gains over GLM-5.2 become, with scores on vulnerability exploitation benchmarks exceeding twice those of GLM-5.2.↗ Blog

GLM-5.3 currently supports text-only inputs, with a 1M-token context window and a maximum output length of 128K tokens. GLM-5.3 always operates with reasoning enabled and supports three reasoning effort levels: low, high, and max. Disabling reasoning is no longer supported. The reasoning parameters are described below:

Parameter

Values

Default

Description

thinking.type

enabled

enabled

Supports reasoning only; disabling reasoning is not supported.

Migration Notice: If your application currently uses thinking.type: "disabled", please change it to enabled and set reasoning_effort to low before updating the model ID to glm-5.3. Otherwise, the request will fail.

For complex tasks such as coding, we recommend using max. An example is provided below:

If you have previously subscribed to a GLM Coding Plan, including an expired subscription, you can currently access the model API only through the OpenAI Chat Completion-compatible protocol. We will continue to improve and optimize this in upcoming iterations.

GLM-5.3 is now fully available, and you can use it with your preferred coding agents. GuideThe new GLM Coding Plan adopts a points-based quota system, providing transparent and predictable usage. Model calls made during off-peak hours, including all day on weekends, consume only 50% of the standard points. Subscribe now: Individual Plan、Team Plan.

For GLM-5.3, we pushed environment scaling toward tasks that look less like coding exercises and more like real units of expert work. The environments now cover a much broader range of production workflows, with tasks designed around how engineering and research work is actually carried out in practice. Some represent several days of work for an experienced engineer.In an ML infrastructure task, for example, the model may be given the same working environment as an engineer, with access to compute clusters, storage systems, internal documentation, codebases, and experiment results. It must diagnose bottlenecks across the training stack, implement optimizations, run experiments, and deliver a measurable end-to-end speedup while preserving correctness. Training on environments at this level pushes the model toward taking ownership of substantial work end to end, rather than relying on users to decompose the problem and supervise each step.As agent capability improves, much of the difficulty in scaling post-training moves from the model to the environment. A useful task environment has to be executable, verifiable, and close to real professional work — and we need many of them, not a handful of hand-built ones. To scale this process, we built pipelines that synthesize environments end to end, and for a subset of tasks, the RL reward signal as well. Research agents collect task patterns from real work and turn them into runnable long-horizon environments with multi-step dependencies and hidden state; a judge agent then attempts each task to verify that it is actually solvable. Verifiers are synthesized without access to the reference solution, while solver trajectories are used to discover and close reward shortcuts. A verifier that passes oracle, no-op, and unsolved-state checks produces a binary reward reliable enough to train on directly.It carries over the RL strategies introduced in GLM-5.2, including SAO with compaction, which helps these gains hold on long-horizon tasks rather than only on short ones. The effect shows up across both coding and general agent tasks. GLM-5.3 improves from 4.6 to 28.3 on Terminal-Bench 3.0, from 46.2 to 66.9 on DeepSWE v1.1, and from 23.8 to 28.5 on Agents’ Last Exam. These pipelines still require a meaningful amount of human-in-the-loop work; making environment generation and verification more autonomous is one of the next steps.Beyond public benchmarks, we introduce Z.ai Code Bench, an in-house benchmark designed to evaluate coding agents under realistic user scenarios. It covers diverse task categories and places agents in complex local development environments. At different effort levels, we evaluate agents along two dimensions: end-to-end task completion rate and fine-grained checklist accuracy. As a private benchmark, Z.ai Code Bench also reduces the risk of contamination from public test sets and gives us a more faithful measure of real-world user experience.As shown in the figure, GLM-5.3 improves both performance and token efficiency. It delivers markedly stronger agentic coding results than GLM-5.2 at every effort level while consuming fewer output tokens. At Max effort, GLM-5.3 reaches 34.5% at roughly 75K output tokens per task, compared with 23.4% at 96K for GLM-5.2. The same shift holds against closed models. At High effort, GLM-5.3 reaches 31.4% at around 50K output tokens, surpassing Claude Opus 4.8 at 29.5% with 120K. GLM-5.3 remains behind Claude Fable 5, which reaches 39.5% at Max effort.

As part of post-training, we introduced vulnerability discovery data and environments into the training mix. We expected this to make the model better at finding and reasoning about vulnerabilities. What surprised us was how quickly the capability continued to develop as training scaled. GLM-5.3 did not simply become better at identifying isolated flaws: it began to reason across multiple stages of exploitation, forming coherent plans for complete exploitation chains.We evaluate GLM-5.3 across three benchmarks covering different stages of vulnerability analysis and exploitation.We evaluate GLM-5.3 across three benchmarks covering different stages of vulnerability analysis and exploitation. On CyberGym, which starts from white-box source code and tests whether the model can identify and validate vulnerabilities by triggering faults, GLM-5.3 scores 84.5%, up from GLM-5.2’s 77.2% — the best result on the benchmark, ahead of Mythos 5 (83.8%) and GPT-5.6 Sol (83.6%). On ExploitBench, which requires deeper reasoning about real vulnerabilities and their exploitation, GLM-5.3 reaches 54.4%, more than doubling GLM-5.2’s 24.4%, while Mythos 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol score 78.0% and 76.5%, respectively. On ExploitGym, which measures how many exploitation tasks a model can complete under time-normalized budgets, GLM-5.3 completes 105 tasks within two hours and 130 within six hours, compared with 29 and 39 for GLM-5.2; budgets are normalized across models using per-model throughput figures, detailed in the footnotes. Mythos 5 remains well ahead at 181 and 247 tasks.The pattern across the three is consistent: the further up the exploitation chain a benchmark sits, the larger the gain from GLM-5.2 — and also the wider the remaining gap to the closed frontier. Capability is growing fastest exactly where we are furthest behind.We then tested whether these capabilities transfer beyond controlled benchmarks. Since GLM-5.2, we have been working with several security teams in China to run our models against real-world codebases. After expert review, screening, and deduplication, the model identified 2,436 vulnerabilities across 269 projects, including 1,097 medium-to-high severity issues. The findings span system kernels, operating systems, browser engines, open-source infrastructure, web applications, and network protocols. Many had remained unnoticed for years or even decades, with the oldest dating back roughly 40 years.This work has since grown into an ongoing disclosure effort. We built the Z.ai Security Disclosure Ledger to maintain a public record of the findings as they move through the disclosure process. The ledger is continuously updated as new vulnerabilities are reviewed and disclosed, distinguishing issues that have already been made public from those that are still under disclosure. For disclosed issues, it records information including the affected project, severity, CVE where available, and how long the vulnerability had remained in the codebase.

最佳实践

模型与产品发布记录

公告通知

原生融入视觉能力，使模型能够主动观察界面、渲染与交互反馈并持续迭代改进，实现代码、浏览器与图形界面的协同闭环。

极致高效混合架构：采用线性注意力与稀疏注意力混合架构（总参 320B，激活 18B），计算量与 KV 缓存较 GLM-5.3 大幅降低。

超越 Coding 的专业工作伙伴：拓展至 Office 文档与金融研究工作流，自主拆解复杂目标、调用工具、检查优化输出。

更强的编程能力：GLM-5.3 的编程能力大幅提升，在智谱内部 Z.ai Code Bench 上较 GLM-5.2 提升了 50%，在包括 Terminal Bench 3.0 等公开基准测试中达到开源模型 SOTA 水平

涌现的网络安全能力：在白盒代码审查与漏洞发现持平 Mythos 5，已联合多个中国安全团队测试并累计发现 2436 个漏洞（1097 个中高危）

支持 1M 无损上下文，长程任务能力显著提升，减少复杂任务中的上下文漂移与目标遗忘

Coding 与长程任务评测达到开源 SOTA，在复杂系统工程、深度调试中表现更稳

真实开发体感显著提升，项目级上下文承载、工程规范遵循与多端开发更可靠

面向企业与开发团队的自助订阅方案上线，延续个人版高额模型用量，并兼容全球主流编码工具

支持席位、权限、用量与预算统一管理，帮助团队实现可追踪、可控制的 AI 编程协作

提供集中账单、统一开票与企业级数据安全保障，默认不将代码、提示词和对话内容用于模型训练

高级版支持首发接入最新旗舰模型及高峰期资源优先保障，带来更稳定高效的团队开发体验

Coding 能力大大增强，长程任务（Long Horizon Task）显著提升，支持一次任务中独立、持续工作长达 8 小时，实现从规划、执行到交付的完整闭环

在自主规划、持续执行、问题修复与策略迭代上展现更强的工程智能，能够完成更长链路的复杂任务闭环

综合能力全面对齐 Claude Opus 4.6，成为首个在综合能力上实现全面对齐的中国模型，并跻身全球开源模型前列

通过 multi-turn SFT、RL 与过程质量评估体系，进一步强化长任务中的稳定性、一致性与 tool use 能力

兼顾视觉理解与 Coding 能力，在更小参数量下实现更优的性能表现，多模态任务处理更高效

细粒度理解、几何感知与空间理解能力进一步增强，复杂视觉推理更准确

强化 GUI Agent、Coding Agent 等复杂任务表现，更适合“看懂环境—规划动作—执行任务”的长流程场景

多模态工具链进一步扩展，在文本工具基础上新增支持画框、截图、读网页（含图片识别）等多模态 Tools

面向 OpenClaw 龙虾场景深度优化的基座模型

强化了对外部工具与各类Skills的调用能力，在多步任务中更稳定、更可靠

复杂指令拆解更强，能够精准识别目标、规划步骤，并支持多智能体之间的协同分工

能够更好理解时间维度上的要求，在复杂长任务中保持执行连续性

针对数据吞吐量大、逻辑链条长的龙虾任务，进一步提升了执行效率与响应稳定性

专为复杂系统工程与长程 Agent 任务设计，实现从代码到工程的范式跃迁

后端架构设计、复杂算法实现及顽固 Bug 修复上展现出卓越的深度推理能力

在代码逻辑密度和系统工程能力上直接对标 Claude Opus 4.5

首次集成 DeepSeek Sparse Attention，在维持长文本效果无损的同时，提升 Token Efficiency

采用自研 CogViT 与 GLM-0.5B 的编码器-解码器设计，连接层实现高效跨模态对齐

基于数十亿图文对的 CLIP 预训练，具备强大的视觉语义与关键 Token 提取能力

模型小、速度快，在手写体、表格、印章、竖排等复杂场景中表现稳定

轻量参数规模下实现了高效的 Coding 能力，任务理解与代码生成能力处于同类模型的较高水平

通用能力同级别最优，在写作、翻译、推理、角色扮演、长文本与审美等核心场景下兼顾质量与响应速度

为 GLM-4.7 的免费版本，针对高频调用场景进行优化，显著降低使用门槛与成本

GLM-Image 图像生成模型上线

首个在国产芯片上完成全流程训练的 SOTA 多模态模型

采用「自回归理解 + 扩散解码」混合架构，模型能读懂指令、补全细节

知识密集型场景全面增强，文字渲染更稳更准（汉字尤其出色）

Coding 能力全面提升，代码生成更稳、更完整，长代码与工程级场景下的一次性交付能力显著增强

Agentic Coding 能力升级，支持以任务为中心的端到端开发

前端与视觉代码理解增强，生成页面在布局、交互与审美上更接近可展示、可直接使用的水平

通用对话与内容生成更可靠，复杂问题拆解更清晰，简单问题回应更直接，整体表达更自然、高效

AutoGLM-Phone AI 手机智能助理框架上线

支持用自然语言自动完成 App 操作任务

具备界面识别、意图规划与设备执行的端到端处理能力，无需人工点击或复杂配置

已适配 50+ 主流中文应用场景，覆盖购物、出行、外卖、影音、资讯等高频任务

支持完整操作指令集，包括启动 App、输入文字、滑动、点击、回退、长按等，实现细粒度交互控制

只需录制约 3 秒清晰语音，即可生成专属音色

支持普通话及轻口音，更好复刻节奏、停顿、语气词等个性化表达

无论旁白、客服、剧情配音、教育讲解，均可保持音色统一与情感一致性

# GLM 5.3

## Z.AI — GLM 5.3

## Model Details

GLM 5.3 is Z.AI's flagship open weight text generation model for complex software engineering and agentic tasks. It uses a Mixture-of-Experts architecture with 753B total parameters (744B excluding the multi-token-prediction layer) and approximately 40B active per token, and is built on the same base model as GLM 5.2 with improvements driven by scaled post-training. The model provides a 1M-token context window with up to 128K output tokens, and supports selectable reasoning effort levels so you can trade latency and token consumption against task performance. Typical uses include agentic coding and autonomous software engineering, terminal and CLI task execution, repository-scale code generation and refactoring, long-horizon multi-step engineering tasks spanning many tool calls, infrastructure diagnosis, and long-context analysis of large codebases. It supports function calling, structured JSON output, and response streaming including streamed reasoning content. For more information about model development and performance, see the model card.

###### Note

Access to this model is limited to eligible customers. For more information, contact your AWS account team.

- Model launch date: October 5, 2026
- EOL no sooner than: Not Applicable, at least 45 day EOL Notice will be provided
- Legacy period: at least 45 days
- Model lifecycle policy: Bedrock Model Lifecycle
- Model EOL date: N/A
- Model lifecycle: Active
- Context window: 1M tokens
- Max output tokens: 128K
- Reasoning: Supported (effort configurable: low, medium, high, xhigh, max; default max)
- End User License Agreements and Terms of Use: View

Input Modalities | Output Modalities | APIs supported | Endpoints supported 
---|---|---|---
Audio | Embedding | Responses | bedrock-runtime 
Image | Image | Chat Completions | bedrock-mantle 
Speech | Speech | Converse 
Text | Text | Invoke 
Video | Video 

###### Note

GLM 5.3 is available through cross-Region inference only. Requests must use the US geographic inference profile (us.zai.glm-5.3) or the global inference profile (global.zai.glm-5.3). In-Region on-demand inference is not supported.

## Capabilities and Features

Bedrock Features

Features supported usingbedrock-runtime endpoint

Explicit prompt caching usingbedrock-runtime endpoint

For more information, see Prompt caching for faster model inference.

Explicit Prompt Caching supported | Min tokens per cache checkpoint | Cache retention (TTL) 
---|---|---
Yes | 1,024 | At least 30 minutes 

###### Note

By default, GLM 5.3 supports implicit (automatic) prompt caching. Configuring explicit cache controls can improve your cache hit rate, and therefore reduce latency and cost, so we recommend using explicit prompt caching. See the prompt caching guide for more details.

Reasoning effort

Reasoning is always active for GLM 5.3. You can trade latency and token consumption against task performance by setting the reasoning effort. The supported values arelow, medium, high, xhigh, and max. If you don't set a value, the model uses max. The values none and minimal are not supported for this model, and a request that sets either one fails with a validation error.

Set the effort with the parameter for the API that you call:

- Responses API —reasoning.effort
- Chat Completions API —reasoning_effort
- Converse API —reasoning_effort in additionalModelRequestFields
- InvokeModel API —reasoning_effort in the request body

## Pricing

For pricing information, see the Amazon Bedrock Pricing page.

## Programmatic Access

Use the following model IDs and endpoint URLs to access this model programmatically. GLM 5.3 is available through cross-Region inference only, so you must use the geo or global inference ID rather than the base model ID. For more information about the available APIs and endpoints, see APIs supported and Endpoints supported.

Endpoint | Model ID | In-Region endpoint URL | Geo inference ID | Global inference ID 
---|---|---|---|---
bedrock-runtime | zai.glm-5.3 | Not supported | us.zai.glm-5.3 | global.zai.glm-5.3 

Onbedrock-runtime, the base URL is "https://bedrock-runtime.{region}.amazonaws.com" and requests must name a cross-Region inference ID — us.zai.glm-5.3 or global.zai.glm-5.3 — as the model. The base model ID is not available for in-Region inference.

## Service Tiers

Amazon Bedrock offers multiple service tiers to match your workload requirements. Standard provides pay-per-token access with no commitment (set"service_tier": "default" or omit the field). Priority delivers the fastest response times for a price premium (set "service_tier": "priority"). Flex provides lower-cost access for flexible, non-time-sensitive workloads (set "service_tier": "flex"). Reserved provides dedicated throughput with a term commitment for predictable workloads; it is set at the account level rather than per request (contact your AWS account team to enable). For more information, see service tiers.

Standard | Priority | Flex | Reserved 

## Regional Availability

Regional availability at a glance

Amazon Bedrock offers three inference options: In-Region keeps requests within a single Region for strict compliance, Geo Cross-Region routes across Regions within a geography (such as US, EU, and APAC) while respecting data residency, and Global Cross-Region routes anywhere worldwide when there are no residency constraints. Refer to the Regional availability by models page for more details.

GLM 5.3 supports Geo Cross-Region inference from the US Regions and Global Cross-Region inference from the Regions listed in the following table. In-Region inference is not supported.

## Quotas and Limits

Your AWS account has default quotas to maintain the performance of the service and to ensure appropriate usage of Amazon Bedrock. The default quotas assigned to an account might be updated depending on regional factors, payment history, fraudulent usage, and/or approval of a quota increase request. For more information, see Quotas for Amazon Bedrock documentation and see the limits for the model.

The burndown rate for Z.AI GLM 5.3 on thebedrock-runtime endpoint is 10x for output tokens (1 output token consumes 10 tokens from your quotas).

## Sample Code

Step 1 - AWS Account: If you have an AWS account already, skip this step. If you are new to AWS, sign up for an AWS account.

Step 2 - API key: Go to the Amazon Bedrock console and generate a long-term API key.

Step 3 - Get the SDK: To use this getting started guide, you must have Python already installed. Then install the relevant software depending on the APIs you are using.

Chat Completions API
pip install boto3 openai

Invoke/Converse API
pip install boto3

Step 4 - Set environment variables: Configure your environment to use the API key for authentication.

Chat Completions API
OPENAI_API_KEY="<provide your Bedrock API key>"
OPENAI_BASE_URL="https://bedrock-runtime.<your-region>.amazonaws.com/openai/v1"

Invoke/Converse API
AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK="<provide your Bedrock API key>"

Step 5 - Run your first inference request: Save the file asbedrock-first-request.py

Chat Completions API
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI()

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="us.zai.glm-5.3",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Can you explain the features of Amazon Bedrock?"}]
    )
print(response)

Invoke API
import json
import boto3

client = boto3.client('bedrock-runtime', region_name='us-east-1')
response = client.invoke_model(
    modelId='us.zai.glm-5.3',
    body=json.dumps({
            'messages': [{ 'role': 'user', 'content': 'Can you explain the features of Amazon Bedrock?'}],
            'reasoning_effort': 'max',
            'max_tokens': 1024
    })
)
print(json.loads(response['body'].read()))

Converse API
import boto3

client = boto3.client('bedrock-runtime', region_name='us-east-1')
response = client.converse(
    modelId='us.zai.glm-5.3',
    messages=[
        {
            'role': 'user',
            'content': [{'text': 'Can you explain the features of Amazon Bedrock?'}]
        }
    ]
)
print(response)

# Moonshot Kimi

Moonshot's Kimi family of models handles advanced reasoning and chat. It supports extended thinking with a visible reasoning trace before the final answer. A single endpoint serves three variants, each selected by setting themodel field in the request body.

### Try in playground

Test Moonshot Kimi in the Runpod Hub playground.

Endpoint | https://api.runpod.ai/v2/moonshot-kimi/runsync 
---|---
Pricing | $4.00–$15.00 per 1M output tokens, $0.95–$3.00 per 1M input tokens 
Type | Text generation 

This endpoint is fully compatible with the OpenAI API. See the OpenAI compatibility examples below.

## Model variants

Choose a variant by setting themodel field in the request body (default kimi-k2.6). The endpoint slug stays moonshot-kimi for every variant.

model value | Description | Context window | Input price | Output price 
---|---|---|---|---
kimi-k2.6 (default) | General-purpose model with thinking and non-thinking modes, agentic capabilities, and multimodal input. | 256K (262,144 tokens) | $0.95 per 1M tokens | $4.00 per 1M tokens 
kimi-k2.7-code | Coding-focused model with thinking mode and agentic capabilities. | 256K (262,144 tokens) | $0.95 per 1M tokens | $4.00 per 1M tokens 
kimi-k3 | Flagship model with always-on reasoning and configurable reasoning effort for long-horizon coding and knowledge work. | 1M (1,048,576 tokens) | $3.00 per 1M tokens | $15.00 per 1M tokens 

To target a variant other than the default, set themodel field to its ID. For example, to use the flagship model, set "model": "kimi-k3" in the request body (or model="kimi-k3" with the OpenAI SDK).

## Request

All parameters are passed within theinput object in the request body.

Array of message objects with role and content.

The role of the message author. Usesystem, user, or assistant.

The content of the message.

The Kimi variant to use. One ofkimi-k2.6, kimi-k2.7-code, or kimi-k3.

Maximum number of tokens to generate.

### id

Unique identifier for the request.

### status

### delayTime

}

## OpenAI API compatibility

Moonshot Kimi is fully compatible with the OpenAI API format. You can use the OpenAI Python client to interact with this endpoint. You can setmodel to any of the three variant IDs.
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key=RUNPOD_API_KEY,
    base_url="https://api.runpod.ai/v2/moonshot-kimi/openai/v1",
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k2.6",
    messages=[
        {
            "role": "system",
            "content": "You are Kimi.",
        },
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": "What is Runpod?",
        },
    ],
    max_tokens=2048,
    temperature=1,
    reasoning_effort="max", # set for adding reasoning
    top_p=0.9,
)

print(response.choices[0].message.content)

For streaming responses, addstream=True:

    model="kimi-k2.6",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are Kimi."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Explain quantum computing in simple terms."}
    ],
    max_tokens=2048,
    stream=True,
)

for chunk in response:
    if chunk.choices[0].delta.content:
        print(chunk.choices[0].delta.content, end="")

For more details, see Send vLLM requests and the OpenAI API compatibility guide.

## Cost calculation

Moonshot Kimi charges separate rates for input and output tokens, and the rate depends on the variant. Kimi K2.6 and Kimi K2.7 Code charge $0.95 per 1M input tokens and $4.00 per 1M output tokens. Kimi K3 charges $3.00 per 1M input tokens and $15.00 per 1M output tokens. Example costs:

Tokens | K2.6 & K2.7 Code input ($0.95/1M) | K2.6 & K2.7 Code output ($4.00/1M) | K3 input ($3.00/1M) | K3 output ($15.00/1M) 
---|---|---|---|---

10,000 tokens | $0.0095 | $0.04 | $0.03 | $0.15 
100,000 tokens | $0.095 | $0.40 | $0.30 | $1.50 
1,000,000 tokens | $0.95 | $4.00 | $3.00 | $15.00

Kimi.title: Moonshot (Kimi) | Promptfoo
Kimi.description: Moonshot (Kimi) Moonshot AI provides an OpenAI-compatible API for its Kimi models — the Kimi K3 and K2 thinking models and the Moonshot v1 generation models. ... - Kimi K3 — flagship thinking model, 1M context ... - Kimi K2 — thinking models, 256k context...
Kimi.content:
# Moonshot (Kimi)

Moonshot AI provides an OpenAI-compatible API for its Kimi models — the Kimi K3 and K2 thinking models and the Moonshot v1 generation models. The Moonshot provider extends the OpenAI provider, so all of its options are supported.

## Setup

- Get an API key from the Kimi (Moonshot) platform.
- Set theMOONSHOT_API_KEY environment variable or specify apiKey in your config.

Kimi K3 requires a successful account top-up of at least $1; see the access requirements.
providers:
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k3

Bothmoonshot:<model> and moonshot:chat:<model> resolve to the chat completions endpoint. If you omit the model, the provider defaults to kimi-k3.

## Available Models

Moonshot's lineup rotates over time — call the list models API (GET https://api.moonshot.ai/v1/models) for the live set. As of writing:

- Kimi K3 — flagship thinking model, 1M context:kimi-k3 (released July 2026). Always-on reasoning, native image and video understanding, and a top-level reasoning_effort control (see below).
- Kimi K2 — thinking models, 256k context:kimi-k2.6, kimi-k2.5, kimi-k2.7-code, kimi-k2.7-code-highspeed. These reason before answering and emit a separate reasoning stream (see below).
- Moonshot v1 — legacy generation models:moonshot-v1-8k, moonshot-v1-32k, moonshot-v1-128k (context-length variants) and the vision variants moonshot-v1-8k-vision-preview / moonshot-v1-32k-vision-preview / moonshot-v1-128k-vision-preview; existing accounts may also see the auto-router moonshot-v1-auto in the list-models API. The moonshot-v1 series and kimi-k2.5 are closed to newly registered users and sunset platform-wide on August 31, 2026.

The olderkimi-k2-0711-preview, kimi-k2-0905-preview, kimi-k2-turbo-preview, kimi-k2-thinking, kimi-k2-thinking-turbo, and kimi-latest ids were discontinued in 2026 — Moonshot recommends migrating to kimi-k3.

## Configuration
providers:
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k3 # flagship thinking model — leave sampling params unset
  - id: moonshot:moonshot-v1-8k # legacy generation model — accepts arbitrary sampling
    config:
      temperature: 0.2
      max_tokens: 1024

### Configuration Options

The provider accepts every option the OpenAI provider supports. Commonly used:

- temperature, max_tokens, top_p, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty
- stream
- response_format (JSON mode), tools / tool_choice (function calling)
- showThinking — set to false to drop a thinking model's reasoning from the graded output (default true)
- cost, inputCost, outputCost, cacheReadCost — Moonshot ships no built-in price table, so set these to track cost. Every override is in USD per token. Moonshot's official pricing page publishes rates in USD per 1 million tokens, so divide each published rate by 1,000,000 before configuring it. inputCost/outputCost take precedence over the flat cost; cacheReadCost prices cached prompt tokens.

For example, these illustrative per-million rates convert to per-token overrides. Check the official pricing page for the current rates for your model before using them.
providers:
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k3
    config:
      inputCost: 0.000003 # $3.00 per 1M tokens divided by 1,000,000
      cacheReadCost: 0.0000003 # $0.30 per 1M tokens divided by 1,000,000
      outputCost: 0.000015 # $15.00 per 1M tokens divided by 1,000,000
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k2.6
    config:
      inputCost: 0.00000095 # $0.95 per 1M tokens divided by 1,000,000
      cacheReadCost: 0.00000016 # $0.16 per 1M tokens divided by 1,000,000
      outputCost: 0.000004 # $4.00 per 1M tokens divided by 1,000,000

Any other parameter supported by the OpenAI provider is forwarded as-is.

## Kimi thinking models

Thekimi-k3 and kimi-k2.x models are reasoning models and behave differently from the moonshot-v1 family:

- Fixed sampling parameters. Kimi pinstemperature (1.0 with thinking on), top_p, n, and the penalties to fixed values and returns a 400 ("invalid temperature: only 1 is allowed for this model") for any other value. The provider therefore does not send promptfoo's default temperature/max_tokens for kimi-* models — leave them unset (recommended) or set temperature: 1. The moonshot-v1 models accept arbitrary sampling values.
- Reasoning output. Kimi returns a separatereasoning_content stream that promptfoo surfaces with a Thinking: … prefix. Set showThinking: false when you assert on structured output (for example is-json) so the reasoning doesn't contaminate the parsed result.
- Token budget. Reasoning tokens count against the output budget. When you leave the token limit unset the provider lets Moonshot apply its server default (32k for K2.x, 131k for K3); if you set one, leave generous headroom for the answer. Moonshot's canonical field ismax_completion_tokens (max_tokens is a deprecated alias) — the provider sends max_completion_tokens for kimi-* models whichever of the two you configure.
- Controlling thinking. The two generations use different, mutually exclusive controls:
- kimi-k3 is always thinking and accepts a top-level reasoning_effort field, which the provider forwards from config.reasoning_effort. Supported values are low, high, and max (the default). Do not send the K2.x thinking parameter to K3 — the API rejects it.
- kimi-k2.6 and kimi-k2.5 support thinking: { type: disabled } (pass it via config.passthrough); kimi-k2.7-code is always thinking. The thinking parameter is K2.x-only.
- Settingconfig.reasoning_effort on a non-K3 model is a configuration error and the provider fails fast with a clear message instead of sending it.

providers:
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k3
    config:
      showThinking: false
      reasoning_effort: max # optional: low, high, or max (default)
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k2.6
    config:
      passthrough:
        thinking: { type: disabled } # K2.x only: turn reasoning off

See the Kimi K3 quickstart and Using Thinking Models for the full behavior matrix.

## Vision

The vision models (moonshot-v1-*-vision-preview) and the multimodal Kimi models (kimi-k3, kimi-k2.5, kimi-k2.6, kimi-k2.7-code, kimi-k2.7-code-highspeed) accept base64-encoded image input using the standard OpenAI image_url content format. Moonshot does not accept remote image URLs — embed images as data: URIs or reference files uploaded to the Kimi platform as ms://<file-id>. Video input is supported by kimi-k3, kimi-k2.6, kimi-k2.7-code, and kimi-k2.7-code-highspeed, referenced the same way after uploading via the files API. See Use the Kimi Vision Model.

## Example Usage
providers:
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k3
  - id: openai:gpt-4o-mini

prompts:
  - 'Summarize the following in one sentence: {{text}}'

tests:
  - vars:
      text: 'Promptfoo is an open-source tool for testing and evaluating LLM apps.'

A runnable comparison lives in examples/provider-moonshot.

## API Details

- Base URL:https://api.moonshot.ai/v1 (global). China-mainland keys use https://api.moonshot.cn/v1 — point at it with apiBaseUrl, since the global and China platforms issue region-locked keys.
- OpenAI-compatible chat completions API.
- Full API documentation.

## See Also

- OpenAI Provider — compatible configuration options
- Kimi model list and pricing

Kimi.content:
# Moonshot AI Kimi K2.6 now available on Workers AI

@cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6 is now available on Workers AI, in partnership with Moonshot AI for Day 0 support. Kimi K2.6 is a native multimodal agentic model from Moonshot AI that advances practical capabilities in long-horizon coding, coding-driven design, proactive autonomous execution, and swarm-based task orchestration.

Built on a Mixture-of-Experts architecture with 1T total parameters and 32B active per token, Kimi K2.6 delivers frontier-scale intelligence with efficient inference. It scores competitively against GPT-5.4 and Claude Opus 4.6 on agentic and coding benchmarks, including BrowseComp (83.2), SWE-Bench Verified (80.2), and Terminal-Bench 2.0 (66.7).

## Key capabilities

- 262.1k token context window for retaining full conversation history, tool definitions, and codebases across long-running agent sessions
- Long-horizon coding with significant improvements on complex, end-to-end coding tasks across languages including Rust, Go, and Python
- Coding-driven design that transforms simple prompts and visual inputs into production-ready interfaces and full-stack workflows
- Agent swarm orchestration scaling horizontally to 300 sub-agents executing 4,000 coordinated steps for complex autonomous tasks
- Vision inputs for processing images alongside text
- Thinking mode with configurable reasoning depth
- Multi-turn tool calling for building agents that invoke tools across multiple conversation turns

## Differences from Kimi K2.5

If you are migrating from Kimi K2.5, note the following API changes:

- K2.6 useschat_template_kwargs.thinking to control reasoning, replacing chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking
- K2.6 returns reasoning content in thereasoning field, replacing reasoning_content

## Get started

Use Kimi K2.6 through the Workers AI binding (env.AI.run()), the REST API at /ai/run, or the OpenAI-compatible endpoint at /v1/chat/completions. You can also use AI Gateway with any of these endpoints.

For more information, refer to the Kimi K2.6 model page and pricing.

Breaking News

# Elon Musk says running Grok AI costs more than it earns

2 min read0 views

Share:

The xAI chief acknowledged that serving the Grok Bot assistant is too expensive compared with the income it generates, as subscribers report weekly quotas running out unusually quickly and questions grow over how the company will balance its costs.

Elon Musk has acknowledged that running xAI’s Grok Bot is costing his company far more than it earns, offering a rare candid explanation for why many X Premium subscribers have found their usage allowances disappearing faster than expected.

Musk made the remarks in a post on X. They came in reply to a user, posting as “DogecoinNorway,” who tagged him and asked whether Grok Bot limits could be reset, noting that many people said their usage had run out very quickly during the week.

Rather than promising an immediate reset, Musk said the cost of serving Grok Bot was simply too high compared with the revenue it currently brings in.

Why users are hitting limits sooner

Over the past week, several premium subscribers on X have reported that their weekly Grok Bot quotas were being used up at an unusually fast pace.

High operating costs are a familiar challenge across the generative AI industry. Advanced models such as Grok Bot, which is built to handle complex tasks and work closely with the X platform, demand enormous computing power and costly server infrastructure.

The service has reportedly grown to around 800,000 paid users. At that scale, the volume of processing needed appears to have outstripped the subscription income meant to fund it.

What lies ahead for X Premium subscribers

xAI has woven Grok deeply into the social media platform as a way to drive premium sign-ups. However, the present revenue model seems to fall short of covering the computing expenses behind the scenes. Musk’s frank comments suggest the company is applying tighter metering and usage caps to stop server costs from climbing further.

The problem is not unique to xAI. Rising computing bills are a major concern for the entire AI sector, and rivals such as OpenAI are also reported to be quietly restricting how much users can draw on their most advanced models in order to save money.

It remains unclear whether xAI intends to introduce new pricing, change existing usage limits or streamline its backend infrastructure to bring costs down. Until a more sustainable financial balance is reached, users who depend heavily on Grok Bot for daily queries may have to work within the strict caps.

#### Release Notes

# Release Notes

## November

November 2

### grok-imagine-image-quality retired

Requests togrok-imagine-image-quality and grok-imagine-image-pro are now served by grok-imagine-image-2.0-low: grok-imagine-image-2.0 with quality set to low, at a lower per-image price. No request changes are needed. usage.cost_in_usd_ticks on each response reflects the lower price, and gRPC responses (xAI SDK) report grok-imagine-image-2.0-low as the model. See the migration guide.

## October

October 27

### Custom moderation controls

You can now set content guidelines on text API requests. Add aguidelines array to a Chat Completions or Responses API request to set how Grok handles content in the nsfw, violence, and profanity categories. Grok follows the guidelines as it writes its response. See Custom Moderation Controls.

October 14

### Grok Voice 3.0 is available

grok-voice-3.0 is now available with Speech to Speech, at the same price as Grok Voice 2.0. grok-voice-latest now points to grok-voice-3.0, so sessions that use the alias are upgraded automatically. The API is unchanged. To get started, see the Speech to Speech docs.

October 14

### Grok Voice 2.0 deprecation

grok-voice-2.0 is deprecated. To upgrade, set model to grok-voice-3.0 or grok-voice-latest, at the same price. See Upgrading from Grok Voice 2.0.

October 2

### grok-voice-transcribe-1.0 end of life

grok-voice-transcribe-1.0 is deprecated and reaches end of life on October 2, 2026. All requests to that slug are routed to grok-voice-transcribe-2.0 at the same price, with higher accuracy. See the Speech to Text docs.

## September

September 25

### safety_identifier request field

You can now sendsafety_identifier, an opaque end-user identifier assigned by your application, on Chat Completions, the Responses API, deferred chat completions, the Batch API, and the gRPC GetCompletionsRequest. It lets SpaceXSI attribute a policy violation to one of your end users rather than to your API key. The legacy user field is still accepted. See the Security FAQ.

September 21

### Grok 4.7

Grok 4.7, SpaceXSI's frontier model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work, is now available on the xAI API asgrok-4.7. It has a 500k context window, text and image inputs with text-only output, and no text output limit. Pricing is $2 / $0.50 / $6 per 1M tokens (input / cached input / output) below 200k prompt tokens, and $4 / $1 / $12 above. Reasoning effort supports low, medium, high (default), and xhigh. On the Responses API, grok-4.7 always returns reasoning.encrypted_content, even when include does not list it. It is also served on the US regional endpoint. Grok 4.7 Fast is the same model and costs 2x the standard token rates, or 1.5x for long-context requests. It's available only in Cursor and Grok Build, not on the public xAI API, and is billed through your plan there. See the Grok 4.7 overview and the announcement.

September 17

### Grok Voice Transcribe 2.0

grok-voice-transcribe-2.0 is now available. Use grok-voice-transcribe-1.0 or grok-voice-transcribe-2.0; the default is grok-voice-transcribe-2.0. See the Speech to Text docs.

September 2

### grok-imagine-image-quality retirement on November 2

On November 2, 2026,grok-imagine-image-quality is retired. Requests to the slug will be served by grok-imagine-image-2.0 with quality set to low, with no change to the request or response shape and at a lower per-image price. grok-imagine-image (1.0) is not affected. See the migration guide.

## August

August 28

### Imagine image API updates

- Auto quality. Thequality parameter on grok-imagine-image-2.0 now accepts auto, and the default when quality is omitted has moved from medium to auto. Auto currently uses low for image generation and medium for image editing. Images are billed at the quality they are served at. Pass low or medium explicitly to pin a specific quality. See Image Generation.
- Five reference images. Image editing now accepts up to 5 source images per request (was 3). See Multi-Image Editing.
- New aspect ratios. Image generation and editing accept21:9 (cinematic widescreen) and 5:2 (wide banners). See Image Generation.

August 12

### Grok 4.6

Grok 4.6, SpaceXSI's frontier model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work, is now available on the xAI API. It has a 500k context window, text and image inputs with text-only output, and no text output limit. Pricing is $2 / $0.50 / $6 per 1M tokens (input / cached input / output) below 200k prompt tokens, and $4 / $1 / $12 above. Reasoning effort supports low, medium, high (default), and xhigh. See the Grok 4.6 overview and the announcement.

August 11

### Grok Bot

Grok Bot is now available. Durable AI teammates that work on a persistent cloud computer, with messaging, approvals, connectors, and routines. See the Grok Bot overview and Get started.

## July

July 31

### grok-imagine-video-1.5 modalities

grok-imagine-video-1.5 now supports text-to-video, image-to-video, and reference-to-video (including optional preset voices), with native 1080p for T2V and I2V. Text-to-video on this model runs as text-to-image then image-to-video under the hood. See Video Generation, Image-to-Video, and Reference-to-Video.

July 29

### Grok Voice 2.0 is available

grok-voice-2.0 is now available with Speech to Speech. grok-voice-latest will route to this model starting August 5, 2026. To get started, see the Speech to Speech docs. For more details, see our announcement.

July 23

### Adjustable VAD threshold for Speech to Text

Speech to Text now accepts avad_threshold parameter (streaming query param and batch multipart field) to tune the voice-activity gate that skips non-speech audio. Lower values transcribe quieter or noisier speech — useful for narrowband telephony — and 0 disables the gate. See the Speech to Text docs.

July 17

### Grok 4.5 available in the EU

Grok 4.5 is now available in the API console for EU users. See the Grok 4.5 overview.

July 8

### Grok 4.5

Grok 4.5, SpaceXSI's model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work, is now available on the xAI API. Priced at $2 / 1M input tokens and $6 / 1M output tokens, with configurable reasoning effort (low, medium, or high; default high). See the Grok 4.5 overview and the announcement.

## June

June 15

### Priority Processing

You can now request higher scheduling priority per request by settingservice_tier: "priority" on text inference endpoints (Chat Completions and Responses). The response's service_tier field reports the tier actually applied, and priority rates are billed only when priority is used. For more details, see the Priority Processing docs.

June 10

### Public URLs and Files API ↔ Imagine integration

- Public URLs for Files — turn any file in your Files API storage into a permanent, unauthenticated URL that anyone can open, embed, or share. Revocable at any time, or set an auto-expiry between 1 hour and 30 days. See the Public URLs docs.
- Reference stored files as Imagine inputs — substituteimage_file_id, video_file_id, or reference_image_file_ids for URL inputs across every Imagine endpoint, with no need to re-upload bytes or make the file public. See Imagine → Files API Integration.
- Persist Imagine outputs to Files — setstorage_options on any Imagine request to save the generated asset to your Files storage; pair with storage_options.public_url to publish a shareable link in one round trip. See Imagine → Files API Integration.

## May

May 29

### Smart Turn for Streaming STT

The streaming Speech to Text API now supports Smart Turn end-of-turn detection. When enabled via thesmart_turn query parameter, an ML model predicts whether the speaker has finished their thought at silence boundaries — reducing false endpointing during dictation, number sequences, and mid-sentence pauses. Use smart_turn_timeout to set a maximum silence fallback. For more details, see the Smart Turn docs.

May 29

### Context Compaction

The Context Compaction API is now available. You can shrink long conversations into a shorter context and reuse it in follow-up requests for lower cost, faster time-to-first-token, and sharper responses on long agent loops. For more details, see the Context Compaction docs.

WebSocket Responses API mode is now available. Drive the Responses API over a single, long-lived WebSocket connection for lower end-to-end latency on tool-heavy agent workloads. For more details, see the WebSocket Mode docs.

May 27

Web Search now supports explicitly searching for images. Enableenable_image_search to let Grok search directly for relevant images; responses can include returned images as Markdown image embeds. For details, see Enable Image Search.

May 19

SpaceXSI's coding model, trained specifically for agentic coding workflows. Currently in early access.

The model slug isgrok-build-0.1.

Grok Build is now available in beta. Use the interactive TUI, run headlessly in scripts, or build apps and orchestrators with the Agent Client Protocol.

Install with a single command:

For more details, see the Grok Build docs.

You can now clone a voice from a short audio clip and use it across the Text-to-Speech and Speech to Speech APIs. Create and manage your voice catalog from the SpaceXSI console. For more details, check out the Custom Voices docs and our blog post.

# Running AI is getting expensive: Why Elon Musk says Grok’s costs are unsustainable

Edited By Abhinav Yadav

Published: Nov 04, 2026, 14:36 IST | Updated: Nov 04, 2026, 14:36 IST

## Running AI is getting expensive: Why Elon Musk says Grok’s costs are unsustainable Photograph: (X)

Story highlights

Elon Musk says the cost of running Grok is too high compared with the revenue it generates. His admission comes as X users report hitting chatbot usage limits faster, raising fresh questions about the economics of AI services.

Running an advanced AI chatbot can be expensive, and Elon Musk has acknowledged that Grok is facing this challenge. The billionaire said the cost of servicing xAI’s chatbot is “unsustainably high relative to revenue”, suggesting that the company is spending more to operate the service than it currently earns from it.

His comments came after an X user complained that Grok’s usage limits were being exhausted unusually quickly. The response has brought a bigger question into focus: can AI companies turn increasingly powerful chatbots into profitable businesses?

Why are Grok users hitting their limits?

The discussion began when an X user, DogecoinNorway, asked Musk whether Grok’s usage limits could be reset. The user said several people had noticed their quotas running out much faster than usual.

Musk did not promise a reset. Instead, he pointed to the financial pressure behind the restrictions, saying the cost of providing Grok was too high compared with the revenue it generated. AI chatbots require substantial computing resources to answer questions, generate content and handle complex requests. Every interaction uses processing power, while more advanced tasks can require significantly more computing. As usage grows, so does the demand for computing infrastructure. This can make it difficult for companies to offer extensive access through fixed-price subscriptions.

## Is Grok's subscription model covering its costs?

## Trending Stories

Grok is integrated into X's paid subscription offerings, making the chatbot an important part of the platform's premium services. However, subscription revenue does not automatically translate into profit. Companies must also pay for computing hardware, data centres, electricity, infrastructure and the teams needed to develop and maintain their models. The supplied context estimates that Grok has around 800,000 paid users. However, this figure does not establish how much revenue the chatbot generates or how much it costs xAI to operate.

Musk's admission suggests that the current balance between usage and revenue remains a challenge. Usage caps can help companies manage demand and control operational spending.

## Is the wider AI industry facing the same problem?

Grok's cost challenge reflects a broader issue for the generative AI industry. Developing an advanced model is only one part of the expense. Companies must also pay to serve it every time a user makes a request. This creates a difficult business equation: users expect powerful AI tools, quick responses and generous usage limits, while providers need to recover the cost of delivering those services. For Grok subscribers, tighter limits could mean fewer queries or more restrictions on intensive tasks. xAI has not, based on the information provided, announced a specific change to subscription prices or a revised usage policy. The bigger test for AI companies is no longer simply building more capable chatbots. It is finding a way to make them financially sustainable as demand continues to grow.

IT Brief New Zealand - Technology news for CIOs & IT decision-makers

# Mistral releases open-weight ML4 for coding & cyber
Tue, 3rd Nov 2026 (Yesterday) 
MARA SUGUE News Editor

Mistral has released the weights for its open model, Mistral Large 4, on Hugging Face, describing it as its flagship open frontier system.

Also referred to as ML4, the model is a 1 trillion-parameter natively multimodal system with 52 billion active parameters. Mistral said it continued training the model for three weeks using reinforcement learning after an earlier preview, while testing it with customers and cybersecurity partners ahead of the wider release.

Mistral said the model ranks as the top open model for agentic coding on Artificial Analysis' Coding Agent Index. It also said ML4 improved its score on Terminal-Bench 4.0 from 28% to 41%, putting it level with GLM-5.3 on that benchmark.

On the Artificial Analysis benchmark, ML4 uses 47% fewer tokens per task on average than GLM-5.3 while delivering similar results, Mistral said. The model also includes three reasoning modes - low, medium and high - allowing users to set the level of reasoning for each task.

Coding Focus

Mistral is positioning the release around coding and cybersecurity use cases, particularly for organisations that want to run models on their own systems. It said the approach could appeal to regulated sectors seeking tighter control over code, data and access.

The model can also be deployed on a customer's own infrastructure for cyber defence work, according to Mistral. That would allow enterprises and government bodies to detect, analyse and respond to threats across software code and IT systems without relying on a third party to maintain access.

ML4 was trained on 3,800 Nvidia Grace Blackwell graphics processing units in Mistral's European data centres, according to the company. It said this gave it a path to state-of-the-art results with lower compute and capital demands than closed-model developers.

Mistral said one technical change since the preview was the addition of two reasoning modes during the same reinforcement learning run.

"ML4 OSS showcases our science team's ability to innovate at speed. Building on the ML4 Preview, the open weight version continues reinforcement learning training and delivers substantial gains with no signs of saturation. In under three weeks within the same reinforcement learning run, we integrated customer feedback by introducing two additional reasoning modes, while making ML4 more efficient and customisable," said Pierre Stock, Vice President of Science, Mistral.

Open Model Push

The release comes as debate continues over whether leading AI systems should be distributed as open-weight models or kept behind proprietary interfaces. Open-weight releases allow developers and organisations to download model parameters and run them on their own infrastructure, although deploying them at scale still requires substantial computing resources.

Mistral has built its profile around open models as it competes with larger US AI groups. In comments on the release, it contrasted its funding with the spending levels associated with some rivals developing closed models.

"Open source is essential to ensure state-of-the-art AI does not end up concentrated in the hands of a few actors. Other labs have raised hundreds of billions to develop equivalent capabilities; in three years, Mistral raised roughly $6 billion. We have taken the lead globally in compute efficiency and have widened the gap between Mistral and other labs in that area. Our approach is to deliver quality science and put the results in everyone's hands," said Arthur Mensch, Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder, Mistral.

Mistral also outlined several industrial uses for the model. It said manufacturing groups could use it to turn two-dimensional blueprints into three-dimensional models inside computer-aided design software, while financial institutions could apply it to spreadsheet work, large-scale data analysis and information extraction from filings.

Its multimodal design could also support geospatial tasks such as analysing satellite and aerial imagery for wildfire detection, crop monitoring and checks on power line infrastructure risks, Mistral said.

ML4 is also available through Mistral's application programming interface alongside the Hugging Face release, according to the company. The launch follows the recent introduction of Voxtral 3, a set of voice models and voice agents, as Mistral broadens its model lineup across different formats.

cross_cutting.content:
# China's Tencent has announced its high-performance AI model 'Hy4' and promised to release it as an open model.

This article, originally posted in Japanese on 12:29 Nov 05, 2026, may contains some machine-translated parts.

If you would like to suggest a corrected translation, please click here.

Chinese IT giant Tencent announced a new AI model, 'Tencent Hy4,' on November 4, 2026. It is said to support image recognition and PC operation, and will demonstrate high performance in a wide range of fields, including programming, financial analysis, game development, and scientific research. Tencent also revealed its intention to release the model weights for Hy4 in the near future.

Tennatural Hy

https://hy.tencent.ai/research/hy4

Tencent Launches Hy4, Joining the Ranks of the World's Leading Open-Source AI Models - Tencent

https://www.tencent.com/tencent-launches-hy4-joining-the-ranks-of-the-worlds-leading-open-source-ai-models/

Introducing Hy4 https://t.co/4mcX5jiUDH
 — Tencent Hy (@TencentHunyuan) November 4, 2026

Hy4 is a large-scale language model developed by Tencent's AI development team, 'Tencent Hy.' A preliminary model, 'Hy4 preview,' was announced in August 2026, and this Hy4 is the official version.
Hy4 preview employs the 'Mixture of Experts (MoE)' architecture, with a total of 770 billion parameters and 49 billion parameters used during inference. MoE is characterized by its ability to run only the necessary parts depending on the processing content, thus keeping the computational load down despite having a vast number of parameters. It also features a massive context window of approximately 1 million tokens.
The official version of Hy4 features enhanced pre-training and additional training capabilities, resulting in improved ability to follow instructions, understand long texts, and autonomously perform multi-step tasks. Furthermore, it is the first in the Hy series to include image recognition capabilities, enabling it to analyze complex graphs and perform mathematical reasoning using images.
Furthermore, Hy4 now supports the 'Computer Use' function, which allows it to operate software on a PC. Because it can handle not only command-line interfaces but also graphical user interfaces (GUIs) operated with a mouse and keyboard, the AI can plan and execute multiple operations. It has also received specialized training in using 3DCG production software such as Blender and CAD software, enabling the automation of complex production tasks.

????Hy4 is here, new with vision.
 — Tencent Hy (@TencentHunyuan) November 4, 2026
 Firmly among the leading open models.
 More productive everywhere: finance, frontend, game, officework, research…
 Built responsibly, with cyber/biosecurity in mind.
 Try it out and let us know!
 ????：https://t.co/ZzL4DtgH3h https://t.co/xceRxN6ueT

Tencent explains that in developing Hy4, they prioritized performance that is useful in actual business operations. For example, in evaluations using their business support tool 'WorkBuddy,' it recorded an average score of 83.18 points and a task success rate of 96.15%. It also ranked first in 9 out of 12 business scenarios compared to AI models in China.
In the financial sector, Tencent's financial technology division conducted a blind evaluation with 213 financial professionals. Evaluating 579 tasks based on actual financial operations, Hy4 scored 3.04 points, surpassing DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017's 2.97 points and Kimi K3.1 Pro and GLM-5.3's 2.68 points. Tencent reported that it demonstrated the best performance among the open models compared.
In the programming field, optimizations have been made to handle complex business logic, state management, and front-end and back-end integration. Furthermore, support for game engines such as Unreal Engine, Unity, and Godot has been strengthened through collaboration with Tencent's game development division. Compared to the Hy4 preview, performance improvements of 19.1% were observed in 'GameDev,' which measures game development capabilities, and 9.8% in 'GameLogic,' which evaluates game logic.
Furthermore, applications to scientific research are also progressing. In an evaluation called 'TenureTrail,' which covered 123 research tasks across 7 fields, Tencent explains that Hy4 demonstrated high performance in areas such as solving mathematical problems, physical simulations, earth and environmental science, and systems engineering. In addition, efforts are underway to utilize Hy4 itself in AI development, and an example has been presented in which Hy4 optimized the pre-training environment for small-scale models using the same architecture.
Improvements have also been reported in the accuracy of the answers. In an internal evaluation conducted by Tencent, the incidence of 'hallucination,' where the AI generates information that is contrary to the facts, decreased from 12.95% in the Hy4 preview to 7.2%. Errors due to insufficient evidence also decreased from 23.1% to 5.6%.
It has also received high praise from external evaluation organizations. Arena.ai, which compares the performance of AI models, reported that Hy4 ranked 14th overall in 'Agent Arena,' which evaluates long-duration agent tasks that closely resemble real-world work. According to Arena.ai, Hy4 is currently a proprietary model, but once its model weights are made public, it will be among the top open models, on par with Kimi K3.1 Pro.

Exciting news from Agent Arena: Hy4 by @TencentHunyuan just landed #14 overall. Currently proprietary, but once its weights are released it will tie with Kimi K3.1 Pro for #1 among open models!
 — Arena.ai (@arena) November 4, 2026
 Across +8.5K real-world, long-horizon agentic sessions from our global community of users, Hy4 delivers +4.7% net improvement and joins the Agent Arena Pareto frontier. At $0.55/task, Hy4 costs about 62% less than Kimi K3.1 Pro (Max) at $1.46/task, and the two models' scores are within 1 percentage point.
 This release is a +3.6 percentage pt improvement from Hy4 preview at #25 with +1.1%. In fact, Hy4 improved across all key signals:
 - Confirmed Success (explicit “yes, that worked” from users): #11 with +8.7% (up from #16 with +4.9%)
 - Praise vs Complaint (sentiment in user reactions): #18 with +3.8% (up from #24 with +1%)
 - Steerability (responding to user corrections): #14 with +5.7% (up from #27 with +0.21%)
 - Bash Reliability (successful shell commands): #20 with +6.2% (up from #41 with -3.1%)
 Congrats to the @TencentHunyuan team on this release!

Plotly, a developer of data analysis tools, has also published its performance evaluation of Hy4. The graph below shows the cost of running all 43 questions prepared to evaluate the AI model's data analysis capabilities on the horizontal axis, and the accuracy rate on the vertical axis. Hy4 achieved a result of 98% for approximately $2.10, surpassing the accuracy rate of several more expensive AI models. Furthermore, it demonstrates particularly excellent cost performance among models scheduled to be released as open models.

The following graph shows the median processing time per question on the horizontal axis and the accuracy rate on the vertical axis. Hy4's processing time was approximately 117 seconds, which is significantly longer than the approximately 18 seconds for GPT-6.1 Sol and approximately 27 seconds for GPT-6 Astra, which also recorded high accuracy rates. According to Plotly, Hy4 tends to repeatedly validate data using numerous queries and graphs before providing answers, and the entire evaluation took approximately 3 hours to complete.

Tencent is also working to ensure security as it moves towards making Hy4 an open model. In the cybersecurity field, the model is primarily trained on defensive data that helps in the discovery and remediation of vulnerabilities, while offensive training data is excluded. The company's security research team explains that an evaluation conducted by the company found no significant concerns regarding the offensive cyber capabilities investigated.
An internal evaluation by experts was also conducted in the field of biology. While Hy4 possesses a wealth of fundamental biological knowledge, its ability to design highly flexible experiments was limited compared to state-of-the-art models. Tencent plans to release a 'system card' summarizing the details of this safety evaluation when it releases the model weights.
Hy4 is already available on Tencent's cloud service 'Tencent Cloud TokenHub,' as well as on WorkBuddy, CodeBuddy, Yuanbao, ima, and others. It also supports API usage through external services such as OpenRouter. A lower-cost version, 'Hy4 Flash,' is planned for release in the future.
While the model weights for the early Hy4 preview model are already publicly available under the Apache License 2.0, the official version of Hy4's weights have not yet been released as of November 5, 2026. Tencent has announced that they will be released soon, and once they are, developers will be able to run Hy4 in their own environments and customize it for specific uses.

# Tencent unveils Hy4 as open-weight AI race with DeepSeek, Z.ai, Alibaba heats up

Tech giant says the new model introduces visual reasoning and powers a comprehensive update to its workplace AI tool WorkBuddy

2-MIN READ2-MIN

0

Listen

Iris Dengin Shenzhen

Chinese tech giant Tencent Holdings has rolled out its latest flagship artificial intelligence model, Hy4, seeking to challenge top open-weight rivals with enhanced agentic capabilities built to power its enterprise software ecosystem.

Released on Wednesday, the large language model (LLM) introduced visual understanding for the first time. Hy4 could process images, analyse complex charts and conduct visual mathematical reasoning, according to the Shenzhen-based company.

Tencent said the release marked the first time its AI line-up became “one of the strongest open-weight models available today”, although it acknowledged that the model still trailed the world’s leading closed-source systems, particularly on challenging internal benchmarks for research-level mathematics, long-horizon coding, model self-improvement and advanced visual question answering.

“We will continue to steadily scale pre-training and post-training to narrow this gap,” Tencent said in a blog post on Wednesday,

The company has been increasing both model size and training data to close the gap with competitors. The Hy4 series features 770 billion parameters – a 2.6-fold jump from the 295 billion parameters in its predecessor, Hy3.

Tencent indicated that its next-generation model, Hy5, would scale further, while a soon-to-come, lightweight Hy4 Flash version would slash task costs.

The company is also laying the foundation for recursive self-improvement in Hy4, expanding its ability to carry out autonomous AI research and development.

Underlining a “co-design” strategy to develop the AI model alongside products used in real enterprise workflows, Tencent said Hy4 powered a comprehensive update to its workplace AI tool WorkBuddy. The model achieved an average score of 83.18 and a pass rate of 96.15 per cent in internal evaluations for WorkBuddy tasks, according to the company.

The launch underscores Tencent’s efforts to hold its ground in China’s fierce AI race, with domestic rivals including DeepSeek, Z.ai and Alibaba Group Holding already challenging global peers in the open-weight landscape. Alibaba owns the South China Morning Post.

A preview version of Hy4, launched in late August, ranked 23rd globally on Wednesday on Code Arena’s WebDev leaderboard – a real-time benchmark evaluating LLMs on real-world coding tasks.

With significantly expanded training data and model scale compared with the preview release, Hy4 improved on its earlier version across 12 tasks spanning agentic capabilities, coding and workplace automation, according to Tencent.

The new flagship outperformed Z.ai’s GLM-5.3 and the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 model across all tested tasks, while trading wins with Moonshot’s Kimi K3.1 Pro, according to benchmarks published in the model’s technical blog.

The Hy4 release also marks another step towards Tencent’s goal of building frontier, state-of-the-art AI models. The company aggressively increased its capital expenditure by 176 per cent year on year to 52.8 billion yuan (US$7.9 billion) in the second quarter to fund its AI efforts, pushing free cash flow into negative territory for the period.

Tencent also moved to mitigate cybersecurity concerns by restricting the hacking capabilities of Hy4 during training by filtering out content related to exploit development, reverse engineering and penetration testing “to avoid amplifying potential offensive capabilities”.

Iris is a Senior Technology Reporter based in Shenzhen. She covers Southern China's tech and internet sectors, focusing on smartphones, robotics, the hardware supply chain, and tech giants like Apple, Huawei and Tencent. Joining in 2018, she previously covered the tech sector across Greater Bay Area and mainland China from Hong Kong.

# IndiaAI Mission unveils 3 homegrown AI models for multilingual, offline applications

Members of IndiaAI Mission, Soket Labs Technology and Research Private Limited, and ZenteiQ AiTech Innovations

The IndiaAI Mission, under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), has released three indigenous artificial intelligence foundation models developed by Indian technology companies Soket Labs Technology and Research Private Limited and ZenteiQ AiTech Innovations.

The models, EKA-1 by Soket and Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B by ZenteiQ, were unveiled at an event in New Delhi on November 3 in the presence of S. Krishnan, Secretary, MeitY, senior ministry, and IndiaAI officials, and representatives of the two companies.

Developed under the IndiaAI Innovation Centre’s Foundation Models pillar, the models are designed for different applications. EKA-1 is an open, sparse hybrid language model with 26.3 billion parameters, trained on approximately 7.5 trillion tokens and supporting all 22 scheduled Indian languages alongside English. Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B are open-source multilingual assistants designed for secure, on-premise, and offline-capable deployment across critical sectors.

The release marks another development under the government’s IndiaAI Mission, which is supporting domestic teams in building foundation models and large language models for Indian requirements.

## EKA-1 targets reasoning, coding, enterprise applications

Developed by Soket Labs Technology and Research, EKA-1 features 26.3 billion parameters and has been trained on approximately 7.5 trillion tokens. The model supports all 22 scheduled Indian languages as well as English.

Built using an open, sparse hybrid architecture, EKA-1 is designed for mathematics, coding, reasoning, and agentic use. Its stated application areas include banking, financial services, and cybersecurity.

Speaking at the launch, Abhishek Upperwal, CEO of Soket Labs Technology and Research, said the company had developed the model with support from the IndiaAI Mission to address India’s sector-specific requirements. “With the support of the IndiaAI Mission, we have developed an advanced AI model specifically tailored to India’s unique banking, financial services and cybersecurity landscape. It is designed to address sector-specific requirements, understand India’s evolving digital ecosystem, and deliver solutions aligned with the country’s needs and priorities,” Upperwal said.

## Dhīr models designed for secure, offline deployment

ZenteiQ AiTech Innovations has also introduced Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B as open-source multilingual models supporting English and 10 Indian languages. The models can be deployed as secure, on-premise assistants, and are designed to support offline-capable, document-grounded automation, knowledge retrieval, and citizen and enterprise services. Their proposed applications include defence, government, industrial, and educational environments, particularly in locations with limited connectivity or where sensitive information requires local processing.

According to the company, the models can operate across different computing platforms, including graphics processing units (GPUs) and tensor processing units (TPUs). Their lightweight architecture also enables on-device deployment on mobile phones, without requiring continuous cloud connectivity.

Prof. Sashikumar, CEO of ZenteiQ AiTech Innovations, said the models allow users to access AI capabilities locally while keeping data on their devices. “Models like Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B offer the flexibility to run across different computing platforms, including GPUs and TPUs. Their lightweight architecture also enables on-device deployment on mobile phones, without dependence on cloud connectivity. This allows users to access AI capabilities locally while keeping data on their devices, enhancing privacy, security, and accessibility,” he said.

## IndiaAI Mission support for indigenous model development

Soket AI and ZenteiQ were selected under the IndiaAI Innovation Centre’s Foundation Models pillar to develop indigenous foundation AI capabilities and large language models.

The government said access to subsidized national AI compute infrastructure and support for ancillary research expenses under the mission helped the teams develop the models. The initiative highlights the role of shared public computing resources and research support in enabling domestic AI development. S. Krishnan, Secretary, MeitY, said the development of indigenous models strengthens India’s technological and strategic autonomy in artificial intelligence and creates opportunities to improve productivity and efficiency across government, industry, research and education.

He also highlighted the role of AIKosh, the IndiaAI datasets platform, in making such resources accessible to researchers, students, innovators and the wider public, encouraging further experimentation and innovation.

Sudeep Shrivastava, COO of IndiaAI, said the mission’s support ecosystem aims to make artificial intelligence more accessible and relevant to India’s requirements. “Breakthrough models like Dhīr and EKA-1 showcase the nation’s multi-layered progress in AI ranging from lightweight solutions optimized for everyday devices to robust powerhouses engineered for complex enterprise applications,” Shrivastava said.

The release of EKA-1 and the Dhīr models comes under the Innovation Centre pillar, which focuses on developing indigenous foundation models and large language models.

With the three models now released, the IndiaAI Mission is expanding the range of domestically developed AI resources available for experimentation and deployment. Their proposed applications span multilingual assistance, coding, reasoning, knowledge retrieval, and enterprise services, with particular emphasis on Indian-language capabilities and deployment in secure or low-connectivity environments.

-- K.ai goes beyond answering questions to executing inventory, pricing, and booking-related tasks in Klook's merchant portal

SINGAPORE and HONG KONG Nov. 3, 2026 /PRNewswire=YONHAP/ -- Klook [https://www.klook.com/], a leading global platform for experiences, launches K.ai, an AI agent that helps experiences merchants manage their businesses by executing everyday tasks in Klook's merchant portal.

Unlike conventional AI assistants that only answer questions or provide recommendations, K.ai can retrieve business information and act on merchants' instructions, from checking bookings and availability to updating inventory and pricing. This reduces the need for merchants to navigate multiple menus and complete routine tasks manually.

K.ai is now being introduced to Klook's merchants through a phased global rollout, ahead of the year-end travel season.

Bringing SMEs from offline to AI-powered operations

Experiences remain one of travel's least digitized categories. According to Euromonitor, only about 34% of experiences bookings are made online, compared with 66% for accommodations and 81% for flights.

A key reason is fragmentation: small and medium-sized (SME) operators make up around 95% of the sector, and many lack the digital reach to sell beyond walk-ins and offline channels. The result is a large, fragmented supply base that travelers still struggle to find, compare and book online.

By bringing these merchants online, Klook makes them discoverable and bookable to travelers worldwide, and by embedding AI into Klook's existing tech infrastructure, it helps them leapfrog from manual processes to AI-powered business management.

"Many experiences merchants don't have dedicated teams to manage technology or back-office operations. With K.ai, we're bringing the most practical and valuable agentic AI capabilities into their day-to-day operations, removing much of the manual work involved in running their businesses, so they can spend more time on what they do best: delivering meaningful experiences for travelers," says Bernie Xiong, Co-founder and CTO of Klook.

From answering questions to getting work done

For SME merchants, managing bookings, inventory and pricing is essential but time-consuming. While most AI business assistants only answer questions, K.ai goes further — it answers questions and takes action.

A merchant can ask, "What did my bookings look like last week?" and receive a report. The merchant can then instruct K.ai to "Raise the weekend price by 10%" and have the change applied in the merchant portal.

Early results from merchants using K.ai demonstrate operational improvements. Tasks that required multiple steps can now be completed 95% faster for individual inventory and pricing updates, and 97% faster for batch checks of products, inventory and orders.

Beyond efficiency, merchants using K.ai recorded 3.4 times as many monthly bookings of those not using the agent. With the ability to adjust operational details in seconds, merchants are better equipped to respond to changing demand and capture booking opportunities.

"I used to block out an hour every morning to update prices and availability across my tours," says Erica Yu, Co-founder of MyProGuide [https://www.klook.com/newsroom/merchant-stories-myproguide] in Taiwan. "The difference is tangible. Now I tell K.ai what I want, and it's done before my coffee is. I'm catching last-minute demand that I used to miss, and I finally have more time to work on the tours themselves."

From back-office operations to business growth

Beyond supporting day-to-day merchant portal operations and queries, K.ai also simplifies other time-consuming aspects of running an experiences business.

With one-click product listing, merchants can upload existing materials and have K.ai generate structured product listings, pre-filling fields for merchants to review and edit instead of building listings from scratch.

K.ai also helps merchants make more informed business decisions by turning customer reviews and performance data into actionable insights.

Through the Reviews and Dashboard pages, K.ai highlights changes in business performance, identifies potential reasons behind them and surfaces opportunities for improvement. This helps merchants better understand customer needs, improve service quality and refine their offerings, shifting their focus from routine administration to growing their businesses.

Source: Klook
