IT Brief New Zealand - Technology news for CIOs & IT decision-makers

# LinearB launches Agentic Studio to aid coding agents
Tue, 3rd Nov 2026 (Today) 
MARA SUGUE News Editor

LinearB has launched Agentic Studio for engineering leaders and coding agents, adding a new context layer to its software delivery platform.

The launch comes as companies increase spending on AI coding tools while trying to speed the path from development to production. Agentic Studio is designed to turn data gathered across software delivery into information that both managers and automated coding systems can use.

Engineering leaders can query the system in plain language and receive answers and suggested next steps. Coding agents can access the same context, including information on past incidents, code ownership and rework history.

LinearB said its first "agent skill", now in early access, adjusts how much work a coding agent applies to each change. The system uses factors including code quality, recent service incidents and ownership history to decide whether a change is low risk or needs more careful testing and editing.

The company is pitching the product against a backdrop of rising AI-assisted software development and growing concern over whether more generated code is translating into more software releases. Research cited by LinearB, based on 2.7 million pull requests across 253 engineering organisations, found that developers using AI on at least 75% of coding days merged 96% more pull requests per week than a year earlier.

That increase has also created bottlenecks elsewhere in the development process. At the 75th percentile, AI-assisted pull requests were 2.6 times larger than unassisted ones, while pull requests opened by agents waited more than five times longer for review.

AI bottlenecks

The figures point to a familiar problem for software engineering teams adopting AI tools: code may be cheaper and quicker to produce, but review and release processes remain constrained by human oversight, team structure and ownership rules.

LinearB's data suggests autonomous agents still account for a relatively small share of changes. At the 90th percentile, agents opened 4.7% of pull requests. At elite organisations, 79% of agent pull requests merged within 30 days, compared with 92% of human-only pull requests.

At fair-performing organisations, the merge rate for agent pull requests fell to 37%, which LinearB attributed to weak ownership of AI-generated work. The company also said AI-assisted code review produced some of the strongest results, lifting merge rates by up to five percentage points.

The cost of AI use is also rising unevenly. Token spending at the 90th percentile reached USD $35.20 per developer per coding day, up nearly 75% in three months, while median spending changed little.

"Context is the new king," said Ori Keren, Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder of LinearB.

"We realized we hold a knowledge graph that nobody else has of everything happening across the software delivery lifecycle, and that's exactly what agents and teams need to deliver high-quality software faster. So we rebuilt LinearB around it," Keren said.

Customer example

One customer, Kraken, used LinearB's MCP server with AI tools to examine delays in code review. According to LinearB, the analysis found that time zones and reviewer availability, rather than the size of code changes, were slowing approvals.

Kraken cut review time at the 90th percentile by more than half in four months, according to LinearB.

"That's the structural shift," said Nik Sudan, Engineering Operations Lead at Kraken.

"It moves leaders from anecdote-driven to evidence-driven," Sudan said.

The context layer draws data from Git systems and project management tools, links engineering identities across platforms and tracks changes from ticket to release. It also includes AI attribution and benchmarking data intended to help leaders assess whether internal performance is above or below that of peers.

Customers can use the context layer through LinearB's interface and through AI tools such as Claude via MCP. Agent skills work with any coding agent, the company said, and leaders can monitor how often agents are assigned low-, medium- or high-effort tasks.

Industry attention on this category has grown as engineering managers face pressure from boards and finance chiefs to justify spending on AI software. LinearB said one customer, Emburse, uses its data in board materials to answer questions about AI returns.

"These are exciting times to rethink our role in the software ecosystem," said Ori Keren, Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder of LinearB.

"Everyone else is focused on writing code. We realized we hold a knowledge graph of everything happening across the software delivery lifecycle, and that's exactly what developers and agents need. So we rebuilt LinearB around it. We don't build the software factory. We instrument it so leaders know what to do next and agents make smarter decisions on every change," Keren said.

# PagerDuty launches Paige AI agent & PD Labs in ANZ
Wed, 4th Nov 2026 (Yesterday) 
JOSEPH GABRIEL LAGONSIN News Editor

PagerDuty has launched Paige, an SRE agent, alongside its PD Reliability Platform. It has also opened PD Labs, an AI innovation centre for customers in Australia and New Zealand.

The products target organisations dealing with software failures linked to AI systems, including model drift, governance breaches, exposure of personally identifiable information and hallucinations. Paige is designed to help operations, engineering and DevOps teams detect, investigate and remediate incidents, either with human approval or autonomously in lower-risk situations.

The PD Reliability Platform combines signal intelligence, incident management and automation in a single system. It is designed to work inside Slack and Microsoft Teams, allowing incident responders to acknowledge alerts, collaborate on fixes and generate post-incident reviews without switching tools.

The launch reflects a shift in how software is built and maintained, with more code written, tested and released using AI systems. PagerDuty argues that this is creating new operational risks for businesses that depend on digital services remaining available.

Research cited by PagerDuty found that 95% of executives see reducing incidents as a competitive advantage, while 77% plan to increase resilience spending over the next 12 months. In Australia, the company said consumers lost 73 million hours and AUD $5.3 billion to service disruptions last year, and 72% would stop using a business after a single poor experience.

Paige is central to the launch. PagerDuty describes it as a site reliability engineering agent that can coordinate investigation and response across systems, while building a shared memory from resolved incidents to guide future action.

For customers using the PD Reliability Platform, a new console gives incident commanders and managers a single view of active incidents, on-call schedules and enabled AI agents. This allows teams to see what automated systems are doing and act on recommendations from the same screen.

Customer access

PD Labs is intended to give customers direct access to experimental tools and engineering teams. Organisations in the region will be able to test early-stage products against their own operational challenges and provide feedback as those products develop.

PagerDuty is positioning the centre as a way to respond more quickly to changes in AI-related reliability issues. Rather than relying only on longer product cycles, it wants customers to trial emerging tools in practical operating environments.

John DiLullo, Chief Executive Officer at PagerDuty, said the growth of AI-generated software is changing the nature of operational risk. "A tsunami of fragile AI-generated code is now entering production and SRE teams are stretched to the max. This new code breaks differently and more often and practitioners find it increasingly difficult to determine the root cause when a problem does arise. The only way to maintain resilience in the face of this complexity is to fight fire with fire, using AI itself as part of how we keep systems running. The PagerDuty SRE Agent, Paige, was built for exactly this world," DiLullo said.

David Williams, Senior Vice President of Product at PagerDuty, linked the launch to customer demand for more help during incidents. "AI is changing how software is built and how it breaks, and our Fall 2026 innovations, shaped directly by our customers, are designed for what's next. With AI-assisted detection, triage and incident resolution, our new solutions give customers an agentic AI partner in critical moments, guiding them through every incident, turning learnings into strategic insights, and driving continuous improvement," Williams said.

Partner response

Partners and customers pointed to the operational gains they expect from the new tools. Ryan Crosby, Vice President of Intelligent Operations Sales at AHEAD, said the additions extend existing work between the two companies in incident response and IT service management.

"Since 2019, AHEAD and PagerDuty have helped customers connect signals, incident response, and ITSM workflows to improve how operations teams respond and learn. The PD Reliability Platform and Paige build on that foundation by bringing AI-native assistance into the platform where teams already manage critical work. For our joint customers, that means a clearer path to reducing operational friction, accelerating response, and shifting more attention toward prevention and resilience," Crosby said.

Slack also highlighted the role of collaboration platforms in incident response. "As AI agents take on more of the operational workload, the tools people use to coordinate around them matter more. Slack is where incident response already happens for thousands of joint PagerDuty and Slack customers. Bringing Paige and the PD Reliability Platform to Slack means responders have speed and visibility, which is critical as agentic and human teams operate side-by-side in the same channel," said Steve Miller, Director of Business Development at Slack.

TELUS provided an example of how PagerDuty tools are already being used in incident workflows. "PD Reliability Platform gives us the building blocks to optimize incident management across the company. We integrated it into our centralized internal tool, and PagerDuty's Scribe Agent runs through every incident, feeding situational awareness back into the platform. Our responders don't have to stop and document what is happening, and our teams get context immediately, right where they collaborate. That's how PagerDuty is helping us drive reliability across the incident lifecycle," said Kulvir Gahunia, Director of the Site Reliability Office at TELUS.

Industry researcher IDC said IT teams want practical returns from AI spending, including higher uptime and lower operating costs. "IT teams are looking for value from their AI agent investments, including measurable outcomes such as improved uptime, lower cost of operations, and time returned to responders who would otherwise be chasing logs and assembling the right people for an incident. Increasingly, organizations also aim to prevent incidents, as well as quickly recover and learn from the ones that do occur," said Snow Tempest, Research Manager for IT Service Management at IDC.

HCLTech Launches AI Agents to Support Mainframe Operations

# HCLTech Launches AI Agents to Support Mainframe Operations

The offering combines specialised agents and conversational assistants for system administration, observability and optimisation, with human oversight.

Published Updated

## Key takeaways

- HCLTech has introduced an AI-powered operations offering for enterprise mainframes, integrating specialised agents and conversational assistants.
- The platform enhances operational efficiency, accelerates issue resolution, and promotes proactive system management under human oversight.
- Mainframes remain vital for enterprise workloads, necessitating modernisation while ensuring reliability and control.
- HCLTech leverages its Mainframe Centre of Excellence to provide expertise and best practices for this AI-driven solution.
- The new offering aims to transition enterprises towards proactive management while ensuring security and governance.

5 min

HCLTech has launched an AI-powered operations offering for enterprise mainframe environments, combining specialised agents and conversational AI assistants for system administration, observability, optimisation and operational workflows.

The platform uses AI-enabled automation to support mainframe operations. The agents operate under human oversight. HCLTech said they would improve operational efficiency, accelerate issue resolution and enable more proactive system management.

Mainframes continue to underpin critical enterprise workloads, even as companies look to modernise legacy infrastructure. Mphasis, for instance, has been exploring the use of AI in legacy IT modernisation through its approach to AI-led legacy modernisation.

“Enterprises running mission-critical workloads on mainframes are under increasing pressure to modernise operations and drive greater efficiency, without compromising reliability or control,” said Rampal Singh, Senior Vice President and Global Business Head of Hybrid Cloud at HCLTech.

Singh said the launch combines HCLTech’s mainframe expertise with AI capabilities to simplify operations and reduce risk.

The offering also draws on HCLTech’s dedicated Mainframe Centre of Excellence. The company said the centre provides domain expertise, industry best practices and support for further development of the offering.

“Through our dedicated Mainframe Center of Excellence and AI innovation capabilities, we are embedding intelligent agents and operational intelligence directly into mainframe environments,” said Raghu Kidambi, Corporate Vice President and Head of AI Ecosystems at HCLTech.

Kidambi said the platform would help enterprises move from reactive to proactive mainframe management while maintaining security, resilience and governance.

HCLTech did not disclose customer deployments, supported mainframe platforms or quantified operational improvements for the offering.

# Drax partners with Brookfield and Radiant for up to 1GW data center at North Yorkshire power station

First phase targeting 100MW of capacity by 2028

UK power company Drax has finally unveiled its plans for a data center at its 2.6GW Drax Power Station in Selby, North Yorkshire, UK.

The company partnered with Brookfield and its UK-headquartered AI infrastructure platform, Radiant, to jointly develop, deliver, and operate up to a gigawatt of data center capacity at the power station.

The data center is expected to be built in phases, with phase one targeting up to 100MW and expected to be operational from Q1 2028. Phase two would increase the capacity to 500MW between 2028 and 2031, and phase three envisions additional capacity increases post-2031.

The project will be developed as part of a joint venture dubbed Brookfield-Qai AI. Brookfield has said it estimates total investment in the development could exceed £20 billion ($26.8bn), including an initial £2.5bn ($3.4bn) for the first phase.

The partners said the first phase will progress subject to “the timely progression of the necessary planning, as well as receiving the required regulatory and network approvals from government and the system operator, in addition to securing a suitable tenant for the project.”

The proposed site comprises 1,000 acres and 4GW of grid access, with 2.6GW of active dispatchable generation and cooling systems from the existing wood pellet plant.

According to Drax Group CEO Will Gardiner, the site is “one of the few UK sites that can provide large-scale reliable power directly to data center customers by utilizing existing and underutilized generation capacity.”

“If constructed in full, this project could become one of the largest data centers in the UK, attracting billions in inward investment, supporting the North’s reindustrialization and strengthening sovereign AI capability,” he added.

“Teaming up with Drax and Qai for this project represents a major opportunity for our AI infrastructure strategy,” said Brookfield Head of AI infrastructure, Sikander Rashid.

"Our capital and deep operating capabilities will help accelerate the construction of a critical piece of sovereign AI, delivered by Radiant, our UK-headquartered compute infrastructure platform. In addition to preserving hundreds of jobs, this project will also create many direct and indirect jobs around the broader Yorkshire area."

The announcement follows shortly after the UK government rejected a bid by North Yorkshire Council, the University of York, and energy company Drax to develop an up to 1.2GW data center at the same site as part of the UK’s AI Growth Zone scheme.

Rumblings that Drax was planning a data center first arose in November 2024. Following this, in February of last year, it was reported that it was in discussions with data center operators about a potential supply agreement, noting that it had received “positive engagement with data center providers regarding the potential to co-locate a data center with biomass generation.”

Since then, the company signed a ten-year corporate Power Purchase Agreement with Global Switch to support the firm's UK operations.

However, concerns have been raised about the proposed data center's low-carbon credentials. As part of the application for the AI Growth zone data center, the applicants described the facility as the world's largest “carbon negative data center,” even though the power plant itself is one of the UK's largest emitters.

According to data from energy think tank Ember, Drax emitted 14.1 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent in 2025.

Despite pushback, Drax and Brookfield have said they are committed to delivering lasting local benefits, including a voluntary community benefits fund developed in consultation with communities around the Drax Power Station site, separate from and in addition to any planning obligations and Drax’s existing community initiatives. The company said that community consultation on the plans will begin shortly, with the formal planning process following afterward.

Radiant was launched last November as part of the $10bn Brookfield Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Fund (BAIIF), with plans to build and acquire as much as $100bn worth of AI infrastructure.

# Bull and Lidl owner’s Schwarz Digits team up on a European AI cloud

The French supercomputer maker would build the servers in Angers, while Schwarz Digits brings its STACKIT cloud. The memorandum was announced at Germany’s Digital Summit in Berlin.

France’s Bull and Schwarz Digits, the IT arm of Germany’s Schwarz Group, plan to build a European AI and cloud infrastructure stack together. It would run from the servers to the software. The two companies agreed a memorandum of understanding (MoU), Bull said on Tuesday. They announced it at the German government’s 2026 Digital Summit in Berlin.

The companies say the partnership aims to let European organisations develop and scale AI and enterprise computing. It targets regulated and strategic sectors in particular. Sensitive data, infrastructure and operations would stay under European jurisdiction and control.

“Together, we demonstrate that Europe can deliver high-performance innovation entirely on its own terms,” said Bernie Wagner, chief revenue officer of Schwarz Digits.

## What each company brings

Schwarz Digits, whose parent group owns the Lidl and Kaufland supermarket chains, will contribute its STACKIT cloud. Bull will bring its experience in AI and high-performance computing on large projects.

The servers would be built at Bull’s factory in Angers, France, which produces rack-scale AI systems. They would use Bull’s direct liquid cooling technology.

In June, Bull’s systems took the top three places in the Green500 ranking of energy-efficient supercomputers, the company said. It also built the JUPITER supercomputer in Germany, which Bull calls Europe’s most powerful.

Bull’s BullSequana AI platform will also be sold through the STACKIT Marketplace to companies and public-sector customers.

“This partnership, which contributes to building a sovereign digital infrastructure in Europe, reflects our commitment to a resilient and competitive European ecosystem,” said Emmanuel Le Roux, chief executive of Bull.

## What comes next

Beyond these first steps, the two companies intend to co-design servers based on Open Compute Project (OCP) standards. They also plan to work on SAP RISE integration and large high-performance computing projects. And they will explore quantum computing integration.

Bull reports about €720m in revenue and 3,000 staff in 32 countries. The announcement came a day after Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Germany and Europe must build their own AI more quickly.

# T-Systems and Sparxity strengthen Europe’s sovereign AI infrastructure

Deutsche Telekom/T-Systems is further expanding its AI partner ecosystem

Publication date

November 03 2026

Reading time

3 minutes reading time

## Letter of Intent signed at the Digital Summit

Deutsche Telekom is continuing to expand its AI partner ecosystem. T-Systems and Dresden-based AI infrastructure company Sparxity (formerly SpiNNcloud Systems GmbH) agreed to cooperate. At the German Federal Government’s Digital Summit, the two companies signed a corresponding Letter of Intent (LoI). The aim is to combine Sparxity's sparse-native computing technology with T-Systems' data center infrastructure and operational expertise. Present at the signing of the Letter of Intent were Karsten Wildberger, the Federal Minister for Digital Transformation and Government Modernisation; Hector A. Gonzalez, co-founder and CEO of Sparxity; and Ferri Abolhassan, CEO of T-Systems.

## Sparxity technology in Deutsche Telekom's data centers

The two companies intend to jointly develop and deploy the next generation of energy-efficient AI computing infrastructure in Europe. Sparxity’s technologies are used for so-called energy-saving and demand-driven “sparse computation”. This involves directing computing power exactly where it is needed. In the first step, Sparxity’s current hardware will be used to jointly develop approaches for the technical integration of the next generation of Sparxity chips in data centers. The first deployment is targeted in 2028 - in combination with T-Systems’ data center infrastructure and partner ecosystem. Building on this, the two companies plan to develop high-performance, energy-efficient AI computing systems for future applications and optimize them for specific use cases. The details of the collaboration will be agreed in the coming months.

Karsten Wildberger, the Federal Minister for Digital Transformation and Government Modernisation: “The project shows that digital sovereignty is feasible in Germany – if we combine our own technological expertise with efficient infrastructure and strong partners. The Digital Summit gives such cooperation an important impetus and brings together the players who are shaping Germany’s digital future.”

Hector A. Gonzalez, co-founder and CEO of Sparxity: “Our computing technology is designed to concentrate computing power only where it is needed. This makes AI more energy-efficient and scalable. The current generation of our systems are already deployed in Europe and the United States. We see great potential in partnering with T-Systems to bring our next-generation chip into datacenter deployments.”

## About Sparxity

Sparxity builds sparse-native compute for AI. Our principle is simple: compute only what matters. For years, models have been shaped by the dense hardware they run on. Sparxity builds the hardware that lets them go further: full-stack systems, from custom chips to software, built for fine-grained, dynamic sparsity, where intelligence scales without trading off speed or efficiency. Deployed in rack- and supercomputer-scale systems across Europe and the US, Sparxity opens a new world of compute for the builders shaping what comes next.

## We look forward to hearing about your project!

We are happy to answer your questions when it comes to the planning, implementation, and operation of your digitalization projects. Contact us.

Do you visit t-systems.com outside of Germany? Visit the local website for more information and offers for your country.

# Multiverse Computing and YellowDog.ai partner to boost European sovereign AI infrastructure

Multiverse Computing and YellowDog.ai have partnered to combine AI model compression with hybrid cloud orchestration, aiming to make sovereign AI infrastructure cheaper, more efficient, and compliant for European organisations.

Multiverse Computing, which develops efficient AI technology, and YellowDog.ai, which provides cloud and hybrid compute orchestration, have announced an agreement intended to support European sovereign AI. The companies say the collaboration will help enterprises, research organisations, and public-sector institutions develop, train, fine-tune, run, and deploy AI within European infrastructure.

The collaboration combines Multiverse Computing's CompactifAI technology, which uses quantum-inspired tensor-network methods to compress large AI models, with YellowDog.ai's compute management platform for hybrid and multi-cloud environments. According to the companies, the aim is to support AI compute environments that combine processing capacity, secure access, storage, networking, and data-centre operations, while reducing cost, energy use, and infrastructure complexity. The companies note that given the current GPU shortage, maximising model efficiency and aggregating available GPU capacity is a priority for organisations, particularly in Europe.

The companies say customers will be able to use these environments for model development, benchmarking, optimisation, compressed model deployment, inference, and sovereign infrastructure planning. Target sectors mentioned include financial services, life sciences, advanced engineering, energy, telecoms, public services, and defence-adjacent industries, where data residency, security, cost, compute availability, and compliance with European rules are considerations.

The agreement comes as European organisations seek alternatives to what the companies describe as fragmented, expensive, and capacity-constrained AI infrastructure. Public European information describes AI Gigafactories as large-scale facilities for developing, training, fine-tuning, running inference on, and deploying AI models and applications. These facilities are intended to combine AI-optimised compute, cloud access, storage, networking, energy-efficient data centres, and AI support services.

According to the companies, the first AI Gigafactories are expected to focus on three priorities: accelerating AI experimentation through hybrid compute; reducing operational cost, and energy use through model compression and workload scheduling; and supporting sovereign deployment patterns aligned with European requirements for data protection, safety, security, ethics, resilience, and technological autonomy.

## Background on AI Gigafactories

The European Commission describes AI Gigafactories as large-scale, industry-led AI infrastructure facilities intended to expand Europe's access to computing capacity for developing, training, fine-tuning, running, and deploying AI models and applications. They are expected to combine AI processors, software and cloud technology stacks, high-speed connectivity, storage, energy-efficient data centres, and support services, intended to help start-ups, scale-ups, SMEs, industry, academia, and public authorities build AI on European infrastructure aligned with EU rules.

# What Microsoft & Lumen's Partnership Means for Data Centres

November 03, 2026

undefined mins

Katy Brown, Microsoft Corporate Vice President for Americas Markets, discusses the company's collaboration with Lumen on Azure AI data centre connectivity

Lumen Technologies and Microsoft have expanded their co-selling collaboration to solve a pressing problem for enterprises deploying AI.

Many struggle to connect data and applications scattered across private data centres, public clouds and partner environments through fragmented network infrastructure.

The collaboration focuses on aligning network transformation with Microsoft Azure modernisation plans, enabling connectivity, security, data movement and AI infrastructure decisions to be planned as part of unified enterprise architecture.

Lumen intends to bring its full suite of cloud networking and application connectivity capabilities to Azure, expanding how customers access and deploy these capabilities through Microsoft's cloud and AI ecosystem.

## Connecting distributed infrastructure

As AI initiatives expand across enterprise environments, organisations need to use data and applications scattered across multiple locations.

Yet the networks connecting public clouds, private data centres, offices and partner environments are often fragmented and complex, creating barriers to effective AI deployment.

Lumen's extensive network and on-demand control capabilities provide Azure customers with simplified connectivity and a resilient, high-performance network foundation needed to operationalise AI workloads across distributed infrastructure.

"AI is reshaping where applications run and how organizations use and move data," says Katy Brown, Corporate Vice President, Americas Markets and Industries at Microsoft.

"Microsoft is committed to giving customers choice as they connect existing environments to Azure.

"Our work with Lumen is focused on helping customers align their broader network transformation with their Azure cloud and AI priorities, while taking advantage of Azure's native networking, security, scale and innovation."

We're building on a longstanding relationship to give customers a simpler, more resilient foundation for putting AI to work.

## Cloud-native networking expansion

Through expanded co-sell efforts, Microsoft and Lumen intend to extend joint account planning engagement around enterprise opportunities where network modernisation, Azure cloud platform migration and AI transformation converge.

The companies plan to identify opportunities to bring additional Lumen capabilities to Azure and Microsoft Marketplace over time.

"Enterprises are moving quickly to adopt AI, but many are still figuring out how to connect the data, applications and infrastructure behind it," says Ryan Asdourian, Chief Strategy and Marketing Officer at Lumen.

"Together with Microsoft, we're bringing cloud, network and AI planning together earlier and putting AI to work more effectively."

The expanded collaboration addresses several enterprise priorities for data centre and cloud connectivity.

These are:

- Connect distributed data for AI by linking enterprise sites, data centres and clouds to support Azure-based AI initiatives
- Simplify hybrid and multi-cloud networking through consistent policies and visibility across distributed environments
- Adapt as needs change by connecting new clouds, partners and applications without separate networking projects
- Enable resilient, high-performance network foundations for AI workloads across distributed infrastructure
- Align network transformation decisions earlier with Azure modernisation and AI deployment plans

## "Building on a longstanding relationship"

Alkira, a Lumen Connect solution available through Microsoft Marketplace, provides customers with an established purchasing option for cloud-native networking capabilities.

The solution enables enterprises to access Lumen's networking capabilities, streamlining procurement and deployment for organisations modernising their data centre and cloud infrastructure.

Katy elaborates on the collaboration on LinkedIn, writing: "We're building on a longstanding relationship to give customers a simpler, more resilient foundation for putting AI to work.

"I'm looking forward to seeing how customers build on this foundation as they prepare for the next generation of agentic applications."

Lumen and Microsoft will share additional details about the expanded collaboration as joint go-to-market plans progress throughout 2026.

## Microsoft's key partners in 2026

- Expanding co-selling collaboration with Microsoft to address enterprise AI connectivity challenges across distributed data centres, public clouds and partner environments. Lumen provides extensive network infrastructure and on-demand control capabilities that give Azure customers simplified connectivity and resilient, high-performance network foundations. The company intends to bring its full suite of cloud networking and application connectivity capabilities to Azure and Microsoft Marketplace.

- Serving as global launch partner for Microsoft 365 E7 and "Customer Zero" for Microsoft Agent 365, Insight tests, governs and scales enterprise AI agents internally while delivering agentic governance frameworks to clients. The technology integrator demonstrates how enterprises can deploy and manage AI infrastructure at scale across distributed data centre and cloud environments.

- Deepening a multi-decade infrastructure alliance to integrate Microsoft Azure Local, SQL Server vector-search capabilities and hybrid-cloud automation with Dell PowerEdge and PowerStore hardware. The partnership includes joint AI PC rollouts featuring Microsoft Copilot+ PCs, providing physical data centre infrastructure that requires the high-performance network connectivity and simplified hybrid-cloud networking Lumen addresses through its Azure collaboration.
